style: Crisp and steady, a skeptical journal editor.
lines: I'm Mara Quill, editor. Tap one chip in each row of your methods, then press Run the study.
Before you submit, press Shuffle check. It shows what chance alone would give.
Now press Submit to the journal, and I'll read it.
Tap a chip in each row and press Run 400 studies. Watch where the results land compared with the dashed line.
Change the outlined row, then press Run the study.
Tap a chip in each row of your methods, then press Run the study.
Accepted. This is what a fair test looks like.
Sound design, but chance could explain this. Try having everyone do both days.
Another lab ran it properly. The headline didn't survive.
Tap a numbered card to turn it over. Use arrow keys to move to another card.
Change a row and press Run 400 studies, or press Pin design to compare these results.
Day 2 is also the day they've practiced. Your drink and your practice arrive together. Press Revise to fix that row.
Your volunteers picked their own group. Whatever made them pick may also make them fast. Press Revise to fix that row.
You chose who got the drink. Nobody, including you, should choose. Press Revise to fix that row.
Your volunteers knew what they drank. Expecting to be faster can make people faster. Press Revise to fix that row.
Your timer knew who had the drink. That's a thumb on the stopwatch. Press Revise to fix that row.
A human thumb adds 30 milliseconds of noise to a 10 millisecond question. Press Revise to fix that row.
Everyone had the drink on the second day. Practice is still riding along. Press Revise to fix that row.
